analysis:
Examined ClusterOnboardingLive.swift BASE lines 1–893 and the bounded patch against the indexed model and supplied T-041 detail. The patch forwards servingScope with planModels and passes request.scope to leader-side planning/adoption (HEAD 272, 276, 600–601); it also introduces planningScope precedence: explicitly named scope, run settings, saved leadership scope, then publicServing. No supported regression is established by this evidence: scope-dependent placement is not itself serving authorization, and the supplied changes do not demonstrate weakened encryption, cache isolation, billing, or attestation checks.
BASE routing restricts forwarding to the currently paired member (228–237), blocks forwarding during private-image qualification (214–216), and locks acting local commands (202–212). Planning restricts copied/downloaded artifacts through servableArtifacts (677–697) and treats private-image qualification separately (630–631, 663–664). These interactions matter to TB-002/TB-011, A-016/A-017 and T-052/T-054/T-056; T-041 cache mitigations are not modified in the visible excerpt.
Integration must inspect the remaining changed planning/adoption implementation and its placement consumer: verify that a peer-supplied scope only selects planning policy, that scope persists consistently into adoption/start, and that choosing local/private scope cannot bypass public-serving qualification or authorization. The complete range map identifies additional changes outside these source units, including BASE 1039–1073; the patch excerpt is truncated. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a missing control or a vulnerability.
